questions.stem: INTERPOL (International Criminal Police Organization) maintains its General Secretariat in which city?

options.option_text: Lyon, France (INTERPOL General Secretariat relocated here in 1989)
Brussels, Belgium (hosts NATO and major EU headquarters)
Geneva, Switzerland (hosts WHO and many UN agencies)
Vienna, Austria (hosts IAEA, UNODC, and CTBTO)

questions.explanation: INTERPOL's General Secretariat has been in Lyon, France since 1989, when it moved from Paris. Geneva (WHO), Brussels (NATO), and Vienna (IAEA) are classic distractors because they each host prominent international bodies — but none of them is INTERPOL.

questions.stem: The Commonwealth Secretariat, the principal intergovernmental body of the 56-nation Commonwealth of Nations, has its headquarters in:

options.option_text: Ottawa, Canada (home of the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association)
New Delhi, India (largest Commonwealth member nation by population)
London, United Kingdom (at Marlborough House on The Mall)
Nairobi, Kenya (venue of the 2024 CHOGM summit meeting)

questions.explanation: The Commonwealth Secretariat is based at Marlborough House, The Mall, London — a royal residence granted for its use since 1965. Nairobi hosted CHOGM 2024 but that is a summit venue, not the permanent secretariat. India and Canada are large members but neither hosts the Secretariat.

questions.stem: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), which began operations in January 2016 with 57 founding members, is headquartered in:

options.option_text: Tokyo, Japan (hosts regular G7 financial ministerial meetings)
Singapore (serves as ASEAN's primary international financial hub)
Manila, Philippines (permanent seat of the Asian Development Bank)
Beijing, China (AIIB was proposed by China in 2013 and launched here)

questions.explanation: The AIIB is headquartered in Beijing, China — it was proposed by President Xi Jinping in 2013 and formally launched there. Manila (ADB) is the most frequent distractor since both are Asian multilateral development banks, but ADB and AIIB are entirely separate institutions.

questions.stem: Unlike the International Court of Justice — which settles disputes between states — the International Criminal Court (ICC) tries individuals for genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity. Where is the ICC seated?

options.option_text: Strasbourg, France (permanent seat of the European Court of Human Rights)
The Hague, Netherlands (ICC established under the 1998 Rome Statute)
Geneva, Switzerland (seat of the UN Human Rights Council)
Brussels, Belgium (seat of major EU judicial and legislative bodies)

questions.explanation: The ICC is in The Hague, Netherlands — coincidentally the same city as the ICJ but a completely distinct body, created by the Rome Statute (1998, in force 2002) to prosecute individuals. Strasbourg hosts the ECHR; Geneva hosts the Human Rights Council. Confusing ICC with ICJ is the examiners' intended trap here.

questions.stem: The African Union (AU), which formally replaced the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) in 2002, has its permanent headquarters in which city?

options.option_text: Nairobi, Kenya (permanent seat of the UN Environment Programme)
Addis Ababa, Ethiopia (the OAU was also founded here in 1963)
Cairo, Egypt (where the Arab League maintains its headquarters)
Lagos, Nigeria (Africa's most populous metropolitan city)

questions.explanation: The AU headquarters is in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia — the same city where its predecessor the OAU was founded on 25 May 1963. Cairo (Arab League) and Nairobi (UNEP) are recurring exam distractors; Lagos has no major international organisation headquarters.

questions.stem: The Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW), awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2013 for its work on Syria's chemical weapons stockpile, has its headquarters in:

options.option_text: Geneva, Switzerland (seat of the UN Conference on Disarmament)
Vienna, Austria (hosts IAEA and the CTBTO Preparatory Commission)
The Hague, Netherlands (OPCW implements the 1993 CWC treaty)
Brussels, Belgium (headquarters of NATO and the EU Council)

questions.explanation: The OPCW is headquartered in The Hague, Netherlands, and implements the Chemical Weapons Convention (opened for signature 1993, entered into force 1997). Geneva is the strongest distractor because it hosts the Conference on Disarmament, but the OPCW is a distinct body. Vienna (IAEA/CTBTO) covers nuclear, not chemical, weapons.

questions.stem: The International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), established in 2009 and comprising over 160 member states, is headquartered in a Gulf city chosen partly to symbolise the shift from fossil fuels to renewables. Which city is it?

options.option_text: Bonn, Germany (seat of the UN Climate Change Secretariat UNFCCC)
Copenhagen, Denmark (known globally for ambitious renewable energy targets)
Abu Dhabi, UAE (chosen for its solar energy leadership and investment)
Brussels, Belgium (hosts the EU Directorate-General for Energy policy)

questions.explanation: IRENA's permanent headquarters is in Abu Dhabi, UAE — a deliberately symbolic choice, signalling that even a major oil-producing nation is investing in renewable energy. The founding conference was held in Bonn (January 2009), which misleads candidates into selecting Bonn. IRENA's presence in the UAE is a favourite hard-level examiner fact.
